source_row.stem: A nurse counsels a pregnant client taking a benzodiazepine about associated risks. The nurse should mention potential risk of:
source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Neonatal sedation, withdrawal symptoms, or floppy infant syndrome, depending on timing and dose of exposure","B":"Guaranteed severe structural birth defects in every case of exposure, rather than a variable, dose-dependent risk","C":"Improved neonatal outcomes overall, rather than the sedation and withdrawal risks actually associated with this exposure","D":"No risk of any kind to the newborn, despite documented cases of neonatal sedation and withdrawal"}}
source_row.rationale: Benzodiazepine use during pregnancy, particularly near delivery, carries risk of neonatal sedation, withdrawal symptoms, or floppy infant syndrome, requiring careful risk-benefit discussion with the provider.
source_row.source_name: FDA Prescribing Information — Benzodiazepines, Pregnancy Risk
